headline: Tawhid Hridoy hits 242 not out to set highest individual Test score for Bangladesh
summary: Hridoy's historic double century in Sylhet rescues the Tigers from a collapse, securing a 30-run first-innings lead against West Indies.
details: Tawhid Hridoy registered the highest individual score by a Bangladesh batter in Test cricket, remaining unbeaten on 242 off 359 balls in the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet.
The right-hander's herculean effort surpassed Mushfiqur Rahim's previous record of 219 against Zimbabwe in 2018, making Hridoy the fourth Bangladesh batter to score a double century in Tests.
The knock was a remarkable fightback; Bangladesh had slumped to 205 for seven at lunch on the third day before Hridoy's charge powered the team to a 386 for nine total.
Hridoy reached his milestone with 19 fours and seven sixes, including a crucial 117-run partnership for the eighth wicket with Taijul Islam, who scored 22.
The Tigers closed their first innings with a 30-run lead over the West Indies' first-innings total of 356, with Taskin Ahmed falling for 12.
West Indies began their second innings at seven for no loss before bad light stopped the day's play, trailing by 23 runs.
caption:
242 not out! Tawhid Hridoy just rewrote the record books with the highest individual Test score in Bangladesh's history.

Tawhid Hridoy registered the highest individual score by a Bangladesh batter in Test cricket, remaining unbeaten on 242 off 359 balls in the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet.

The right-hander's herculean effort surpassed Mushfiqur Rahim's previous record of 219 against Zimbabwe in 2018, making Hridoy the fourth Bangladesh batter to score a double century in Tests.

The knock was a remarkable fightback; Bangladesh had slumped to 205 for seven at lunch on the third day before Hridoy's charge powered the team to a 386 for nine total.

Hridoy reached his milestone with 19 fours and seven sixes, including a crucial 117-run partnership for the eighth wicket with Taijul Islam, who scored 22.

The Tigers closed their first innings with a 30-run lead over the West Indies' first-innings total of 356, with Taskin Ahmed falling for 12.

West Indies began their second innings at seven for no loss before bad light stopped the day's play, trailing by 23 runs.

headline: 7 Bangladeshis killed in Saudi road crash
summary: The victims, including women and children, were returning to Jeddah from Medina when a truck rammed their bus from behind.
details: The Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah has confirmed that seven Bangladeshis died in a road accident in Saudi Arabia. The victims included women and children.
The crash occurred late Friday night as the group was traveling from Medina back to Jeddah.
Among the dead are storekeeper Ziaur Rahman, his two sons and daughter, storekeeper Alam Shah, and his one-month-old daughter.
The seventh victim was the wife of forklift driver Md Elias. Two employees of Al-Abir Cold Store and four of their relatives were among those killed.
A truck rammed the bus carrying the Bangladeshis from behind, causing the fatal collision.
The bodies have been kept in a local hospital morgue, where 15 injured passengers have also been admitted for treatment.
